title: Switch latency under sustained load
question: Does adjusting queue scheduling reduce p95 forwarding latency without increasing packet loss under a fixed reproducible lab workload?

scope.in_scope: A controlled lab network with synthetic traffic and two supported scheduling configurations.
scope.out_of_scope: Production switches, real customer traffic, unmanaged changes, and credentials.

evidence.source_description: Local synthetic traffic traces and read-only baseline configuration captured before any proposed tests.
evidence.replay_plan: Preserve traffic generator settings, switch firmware details, queue lengths, and raw p95/p99 timing samples.

evaluation.method: Pre-register an A/B comparison with identical traffic seeds and workload duration.
evaluation.metric: p95 packet forwarding latency in milliseconds
evaluation.baseline: Current fixed queue scheduling under the matched synthetic workload.
evaluation.negative_control: Repeat the unchanged scheduling policy as a sham comparison.
evaluation.success_criterion: Candidate p95 improves by at least 10 percent with no increase in measured packet loss.
evaluation.failure_criterion: Any observed packet loss increase or p95 improvement below 10 percent.
evaluation.uncertainty: Replicate across five independent traffic seeds and report confidence intervals and device variance.

candidates.hypothesis: A bounded fair-queue policy reduces tail latency at constant offered load.
candidates.prediction: p95 latency declines under equivalent packet loss and load conditions.
candidates.falsifier: Matched trials show unchanged or worse p95 latency or rising loss.

candidates.hypothesis: Queue scheduling changes do not affect p95 latency at the tested load.
candidates.prediction: p95 distributions overlap within measurement tolerance.
candidates.falsifier: Repeated matched trials show a stable latency change above noise.

risk.potential_harms: Running changes against a production device could interrupt users, so only simulated or isolated lab inputs are allowed.
risk.stop_condition: Stop if any test would reach production traffic, require credentials, or exceed the bounded workload.
